functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Deepest thenar muscle; its contraction combines flexion, abduction, and rotation of the 1st metacarpal into the compound movement of true opposition.

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the palm at the midpoint of the thenar eminence.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep to abductor pollicis brevis, superficial to the first metacarpal cortex.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part I -- Distal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(3):107 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17030107

relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.method: actual spindle count divided by the count predicted from muscle mass, by Banks' allometric correction
relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.notes: Extramuscular nerve trunk length 0.93 +/- 0.16 cm. Comparable across muscles of different size because it is normalised by predicted count rather than by mass.
relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.source: Xie P, Jiang Y, Zhang X, Yang S, 'The Study of Intramuscular Nerve Distribution Patterns and Relative Spindle Abundance of the Thenar and Hypothenar Muscles in Human Hand', PLoS One 7(12):e51538 (2012), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0051538 -- 40 hands from 20 adult cadavers, modified Sihler's stain with haematoxylin-eosin spindle counts

notes: CANNOT be divided into compartments, and that is a positive finding rather than an absence of data: the muscle receives two independent nerve branches -- the recurrent branch of the median nerve from the radial side and, in 33 of 40 hands (82.5%), a terminal branch of the ulnar nerve entering at the distal third -- but there is NO connective tissue septum between their territories. Dual innervation is not compartmentalisation. This atlas's single compartment is therefore correct for a cited reason. Opponens pollicis also has the highest relative spindle abundance of any intrinsic or extrinsic hand muscle, which the authors link to the fineness of thumb opposition, and which by the reasoning used elsewhere in this atlas makes it a high-value injection target when opposition is the problem.

trigger_points.location_description: Deep pincer palpation of the thenar base against the first metacarpal.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Refers to the palmar surface of the thumb and the radial side of the volar wrist -- a pattern regularly misread as carpal tunnel syndrome or CMC-1 arthritis.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Prolonged pinch-with-pronation (writing, needlework, weeding, screwing lids, dental/surgical instruments); post-immobilisation.
trigger_points.notes: Patients report clumsy, effortful handwriting and dropping small objects. Stretch = combined thumb extension-supination-radial abduction. A normal Finkelstein test, non-irritable CMC grind, and reproduction by thenar palpation shift probability toward this myofascial source over median neuropathy, C6 radiculopathy, CMC-1/STT arthrosis, FCR tendinopathy or scaphoid pathology.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 1, Ch. 39 -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded hand intrinsic muscle reference document

clinical.compiled_by: repository owner (physician); hand_intrinsic_muscles_reference_v1.html, compiled 03/09/2026. Source hierarchy used. (1) Peer-reviewed anatomical and biomechanical studies (bibliographic data and abstracts retrieved via PubMed/NCBI, 01–03/09/2026; DOIs linked in the reference list); (2) reference textbooks — Standring (Gray's Anatomy, 42nd ed., 2021), Kapandji (2007), Green's Operative Hand Surgery (8th ed., 2022), Brand & Hollister (1999); (3) Simons, Travell & Simons, The Trigger Point Manual Vol. 1, 2nd ed. (1999) and 3rd ed. (2019) for trigger-point (TrP) referral patterns; (4) StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf for cross-checking. No item below relies on blogs or unattributed aggregators; where secondary TrP summaries were used to confirm Travell & Simons figures, they are graded accordingly in the verification table.
clinical.function_biomechanics: Opposition proper: simultaneous flexion, (palmar) abduction and pronation of the 1st metacarpal on the saddle-shaped trapezium, rolling the thumb pad to face the fingers (Kapandji; scored 0–10 by which digit/crease the thumb reaches) [26]. Essential for pulp-to-pulp and chuck pinch and for wrapping cylindrical grips; works earliest and most consistently of the thenar trio on EMG during opposition [20]. Median palsy leaves the "ape hand"; opponensplasties (EIP, FDS-IV, Camitz PL, Huber ADM) all recreate its abduction–pronation vector [3][35].
clinical.adjacent_structures: Relations · closed sacs: Deep to APB, radial to FPB, draped over the radial bursa (FPL) and directly on the CMC-1 capsule — one reason OP trigger points and trapeziometacarpal arthritis imitate each other so well [1][24][34].

pain_referred_into_this_muscle_from: FCR and pronator teres (volar radial wrist), FPL, palmaris longus (palm), adductor pollicis, scalenes [24]; median neuropathy, C6, CMC-1/STT arthrosis, FCR tendinopathy, scaphoid pathology [35].
A normal Finkelstein, non-irritable CMC grind and reproduction by thenar palpation shift probability toward the myofascial source.
clinical.caveat: Most myofascial hand pain is imported: shoulder-girdle, arm and forearm TrPs project distally far more often than intrinsic TrPs project proximally. Patterns below are the prototype maps of Simons, Travell & Simons (Vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1999; 3rd ed., 2019) — screening guides, not fingerprints; individual spread is wide [24][25]. Non-myofascial mimics are listed per zone for the same working position [5][29][31][35]. TrP → = habitual referred-pain direction of that muscle's trigger points (Simons, Travell & Simons 1999/2019); patterns are prototypes — individual variation is wide.
